tob-10465: John Calvin’s Institutes is the founding text of Reformed Protestantism and one of the most influential books of the Reformation. This first volume lays out his system of doctrine: the nature of God, the authority of Scripture, and the sovereignty of divine grace. Written with lawyer-like precision, it trained generations of pastors and theologians in the Calvinist tradition.
tob-10565: Gertrude Bell’s Hafiz gives the Persian master’s wine-songs and love-lyrics in English verse — poems where the wine-house stands for the soul’s ache and the fair one for God. Wrought ere her desert fame, her versions stay among the most tuneful Hafiz in English.
tob-4165: George Cox’s second Aryan-myth volume bears on with his bold sun-theory of tale — reading gods as sun, dawn, and storm made into persons. His matching way was daring for 1870. The work shows Victorian bookmen grappling with legend’s springs. A bright window on young tale-matching lore.
tob-4265: John Ferguson’s Chemic Book-hoard — book two — lists James Young’s great gathering of gold-books. The book-list is the ground of gold-lore’s book-story. Ferguson’s notes are a treasure of learning. The work stays the needful guide to early chemic letters.
cia-0000102965: Marked with an estimated date of November 1985, this assessment updates what the CIA knew about the whole Soviet forced-labor system. It draws together reports from individual camps into a bigger picture of scale and organization. Updates like this kept American policymakers current on a system that touched mining, construction, and industry across the USSR.
cia-0000106265: A June 1965 intelligence report, its subject line partially garbled in the archive, on resistance efforts along the border between North Vietnam and Laos. The Ho Chi Minh Trail ran through this region, feeding the war in the south. Even with a damaged title, the entry preserves evidence of how the CIA tracked communist supply lines.
cia-0000109065: Estimated to date from November 1968, this report records a Cuban official's views on the future of Cuban-American relations. Even at the height of hostility, back channels and private opinions hinted at what might be possible. The document preserves one insider's reading of a frozen conflict — valuable precisely because such candor was rare.
cia-0000119765: An October 1956 roundup of reactions to the Polish and Hungarian developments — how the world responded to Eastern Europe's upheaval. Governments condemned, publics marched, and Moscow calculated. The document tallies the global echo of two small nations' defiance.
cia-0000124265: A July 1959 report, its title garbled, on Soviet research and development in very-low-frequency radio communications. VLF radio could reach submarines deep underwater — a strategic prize. The document tracks a quiet corner of the arms race: talking to subs that no one could see.
cia-0000126865: An April 1965 report titled Tanzania Taking the Left Turn. Nyerere's Tanzania was embracing African socialism — nationalizations, collectivization, and non-alignment with a leftist tilt. The document watches a new nation's ideology crystallize, through Cold War eyes.
cia-0000126965: A November 1965 report on hard-line dissidents revolting against the established leadership of Venezuela's FALN guerrillas — the truncated title cuts off the rest. Revolutionaries were splitting over how revolutionary to be. The document is a front-row seat to the left eating its own.
cia-0000132165: Situation Report 482 on reactions to Iraq's missile attacks — Scuds falling on Israel and Saudi Arabia, the truncated title suggests. Saddam's missiles were meant to shatter the coalition. The document tracks the political shockwaves of weapons aimed at civilians.
cia-0000132265: Situation Report 572: Saddam's cease-fire bid — less than meets the eye, the title warns. The Iraqi offer came with conditions that meant surrender in disguise, or defiance in disguise. The document dissects the proposal: the fine print behind the headline.
cia-0000132665: A 1960 report: a Salvadoran communist reportedly seeking Cuban support. The isthmus's left looked to Havana for help. The document is the appeal: the Salvadoran, asking.
cia-0000134265: Item 12 in a 1960 Latin America series: the persistence of guerrilla action apparently bothering Castro — the archive's spelling says perisitence. The revolution faced its own rebels. The document is the irony: the guerrilla leader, troubled by guerrillas.
cia-0000136265: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for LANGEVIN with instruction 13 for broadcasts. The unlucky number, dutifully issued. The entry is the instruction: the broadcasts, directed — number thirteen.
cia-0000136865: A 1954 cable to the chief of station at LINCOLN on available channels and message handling — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The communications, organized. The document is the plumbing: the channels, listed.
cia-0000136965: A 1954 cable on a radio newscast at 1716 on June 20 from New York City. The broadcast, logged. The document is the newscast: the time, noted.
cia-0000137465: A 1962 file on the president's trip to Venezuela and Colombia. Kennedy's South American tour — the Alliance for Progress, sold in person. The document is the trip: the president, traveling.
cia-0000141165: A 1961 transmittal of documents with attachments A and B titled Narrative of Air Action — the archive's spelling says narrativee, the truncated title cuts off the rest. The air war's story, forwarded. The entry is the transmittal: the narrative, attached — through a typo.
un-ga-res-a-69-65: Resolution A/69/65, adopted in 2014 during the 69th session. The Assembly's numbered business. The designation and year are preserved; the decision is in the text.
un-ga-res-2065: General Assembly Resolution 2065, adopted in December 1965 — the text inviting Britain and Argentina to negotiate over the Falkland Islands, or Malvinas, recognizing the sovereignty dispute. It became the legal foundation of Argentina's claim, cited in every negotiation since. The resolution is the invitation: the islands, to be discussed.
un-sc-res-65: Security Council Resolution 65, adopted in 1948. The deliberations continued. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-465: Security Council Resolution 465, cataloged with the year 1967 — though the well-known settlements resolution of that number belongs to 1980, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned — and the subject is left to the text.
un-sc-res-665: Security Council Resolution 665, adopted in August 1990 — the naval enforcement resolution, authorizing states to halt shipping and enforce the Iraq sanctions at sea. The blockade took legal form. The resolution is the blockade: the ships, stopped.
un-sc-res-1365: Security Council Resolution 1365, cataloged with the year 1973 — the numbering belongs to 2001, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1465: Security Council Resolution 1465, adopted in 2003 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1565: Security Council Resolution 1565, cataloged with the year 2003 — the historical record places this Congo force-expansion resolution in October 2004, enlarging the UN mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The designation is kept; the catalog's date is questioned.
cia-0000132565: A 1960 CIA file titled Cuban Developments, numbered 0000132565. The revolution's course, tracked as it happened. The document is the development: the island, changing.
cia-0000132765: A 1960 CIA file on Cuba, numbered 0000132765. The archive number distinguishes it from its twins. The document is the distinction: the file, numbered.
cia-0000136565: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136565. The exiles wrote; the agency filed. The entry is the filing: the papers, ordered.
cia-0000136765: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136765, date approximate. The roughly dated papers. The document is the roughness: the date, estimated.
un-ga-res-a-67-265: General Assembly Resolution A/67/265, cataloged with the year 1946 — the numbering belongs to 2013, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d65: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, October 27, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 65. London's letter. The message is the correspondence: the prime minister, writing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d165: A memorandum by the Secretary of State — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 165. Hull's thinking, on paper. The memo is the thinking: the secretary, writing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d265: Combined Chiefs of Staff minutes, November 24, 1943 — Document 265. A second Allied session. The minutes are the second: the planners, returning.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d365: Bohlen minutes, November 29, 1943 — Document 365. The diplomat minuted on. The minutes are the continuation: Bohlen, recording.
arxiv-2605-08765: Telling a language model to forget something — a copyrighted passage, private data — only matters if the forgetting is real. Renjie Gu, Jiazhen Du, Yihua Zhang, and Sijia Liu argue that today's unlearning methods can lie, looking compliant while secretly retaining the banned knowledge. Their paper designs tests for that honesty and proposes unlearning techniques meant to survive scrutiny.
arxiv-2605-08865: Dirichlet L-functions sit at the heart of analytic number theory, encoding deep secrets about prime numbers. Qiyu Yang and Shengbo Zhao prove Omega results — lower bounds showing these functions must sometimes grow large — for the family. The 2026 paper is pure mathematics, charting how wild these fundamental objects can get.
arxiv-2605-09065: Scene graphs describe an image as objects plus their relationships — cup on table, dog near door. Rajalaxmi Rajagopalan and Romit Roy Choudhury generate them with dependency-aware discrete diffusion, respecting how the relationships depend on each other. The 2026 paper is structured vision: images as graphs.
arxiv-2605-09165: Looped language models reuse the same layers repeatedly instead of stacking new ones — but scaling them is tricky. Ryan Lee, Jacob Biloki, Edward J. Hu, and Jonathan May find that sparse layers are critical to making the loops scale. The 2026 paper is architecture research for leaner, deeper models.
arxiv-2605-09365: Not every enterprise job needs a giant language model — and forcing one in wastes money and reliability. Kuldeep Singh, Anson Bastos, and Isaiah Onando Mulang' argue against overstretching LLMs for every enterprise task. The 2026 paper is a position piece: use the right tool, not the biggest.
arxiv-2605-09765: Clinical labels in electronic health records are noisy; multi-view consistency can clean the learned representations anyway. Ruan Dong, Yuanyun Zhang, and Shi Li learn clinical representations from noisy supervision with WISTERIA. The 2026 paper is medical AI that tolerates messy labels.
plos-pone-0003465: Immunologists mapped the immune system's self-pruning in this 2008 paper. The Fas pathway orders damaged or excess T cells to die, and the team showed it constantly trims the peripheral alpha-beta T cell pool, shaping which T cells survive. That ongoing culling keeps the immune repertoire balanced and is a bulwark against autoimmunity.
plos-pone-0003565: Blood researchers found a brake on platelet-maker precursors in this 2008 paper. The phosphatase SHIP-1, which dials down signals from cytokine receptors, restrained early megakaryocyte progenitors, the cells that become platelet factories. Lifting or pressing that brake could matter for disorders of too many or too few platelets.
plos-pone-0003665: In 2008, a team studied gene teamwork behind whooping cough shots. The state of genes in the Toll-like receptor pathway tracked with how strongly children built defenses after pertussis shots. The result shows protection rests not on single genes but on the immune wiring as a whole.
plos-pone-0003765: Zhou, Enyeart, and Wilke built a detector for mutation hotspots in this 2008 paper. When selection favors a protein's function, mutations cluster in small DNA stretches. Their statistical method finds those clusters, separating the fingerprints of adaptation from random noise.
plos-pone-0003865: A 2008 study found yeast cells reading love letters with precision. Moore, Chou, and Nie tested how budding yeast sense mating pheromone gradients across their surface. The robust spatial sensing shows single cells navigating by smell with remarkable accuracy.
plos-pone-0003965: In 2008, Hausmann, Marq, and Tapparel traced how cells sense viral RNA. RIG-I detection of double-stranded RNA was shown driving interferon-beta activation. The pathway map details the tripwire that alerts cells to RNA virus invasion.
plos-pone-0004065: In 2008, Sueur, Pavoine, and Hamerlynck listened hard for biodiversity. Their rapid acoustic survey read species richness from soundscapes. Recording animal calls proved a fast stand-in for slow field counts. The neat method gives conservation a quick ear on the wild.
plos-pone-0004165: In 2009, Herz, Woodfield, and Chen compared sibling sorting genes in flies. ESCRT-II components showed common and distinct genetic roles in fruit flies. The protein-sorting machinery's parts diverged oddly in the fly. The split map refines the sorting-complex story for flies.
plos-pone-0004365: In 2009, a team found probiotics calming gut alarms. Probiotic bacteria blocked IP secretion in human intestinal cells. The VSL mixture's calming trick was mapped fully. The finding supports probiotics for bowel disease care. The post-translational block is a new mechanism indeed.
plos-pone-0351265: When human metapneumovirus surged, public anxiety surged with it. This paper applied explainable AI — built on the XLNet language model — to analyze public sentiment about HMPV. The explanations show which words and phrases drive fear or calm, giving health communicators a live read on the public mood.
plos-pone-0342965: Rural emergency rooms in Québec run on fumes — and patients pay the price. This mixed-methods analysis mapped barriers and priorities for equitable emergency care across rural Québec. The 360° view gives health planners a ranked list of what rural ERs need first.
plos-pone-0358465: Sand behaves strangely under buildings — it can expand when sheared, a quirk called dilatancy. This paper built a state-dependent dilatancy constitutive model with parametric analysis for dense sand–structure interfaces. The model helps engineers predict how foundations grip, settle, and slip under load.
plos-pone-0358565: Soccer players favor one leg — and the imbalance invites injury. This study compared unilateral single-mode balance training against combined balance-plus-plyometric training on interlimb asymmetry in soccer players. The results show which program evens out the legs best for safer, stronger play.
plos-pone-0357965: Flickering light at theta rhythm might coax the brain to rebuild myelin. This study tested non-invasive visual theta entrainment on myelin-related and functional outcomes in an LPC-induced demyelination model. The entrainment improved outcomes — a drug-free lead for repairing the brain’s insulation.
plos-pone-0357765: After rotator cuff repair, the shoulder blade’s stamina matters as much as the cuff itself. This cross-sectional mediation analysis linked scapular endurance and dyskinesis to functional outcomes after repair. The findings tell rehab specialists where to focus recovery: the blade, not just the repaired tendon.
plos-pone-0353165: The sable — Siberia’s prized fur-bearer — has a deeper past than assumed. This paper reported the first Boreal Sable in Pleistocene Arctic Siberia. The ancient specimen rewrites where this iconic mustelid roamed during the Ice Age, extending its known range into the far north.
plos-pone-0358265: China’s level-II peacekeeping hospital in the Democratic Republic of the Congo treats more than battlefield trauma. This case study analyzed trends in the spectrum of oral diseases seen at the hospital. The dental data show what peacekeepers and local civilians alike suffer — and what a field hospital in a conflict zone must be stocked to handle.
plos-pone-0358065: Simulating how worms crawl in three dimensions has uses from biology to soft robotics. This paper presented a mathematical model for worm path simulation in 3D. The equations capture the wriggle faithfully, giving researchers a virtual worm for experiments that real ones won’t sit still for.
plos-pone-0357565: Hypermobile EDS brings a bewildering mix of symptoms that defy simple categories. This paper explored cross-category relationships between symptoms in people with hypermobile EDS to identify disability patterns. The resulting symptom map helps patients and doctors finally see the whole disabling picture at once.
plos-pone-0355465: Appearance-focused social media warps how we see ourselves — and the mood pays the price. This paper studied the impact of appearance-focused social media and self-objectification on mood. The findings quantify the mirror’s toll, showing how curated images translate into real emotional harm.
plos-pone-0357365: PARP inhibitor drugs usually require BRCA mutations to work — but a new player may widen their reach. This integrative proteomics study revealed that MSH6 modulates PARP inhibitor sensitivity in BRCA1/2-proficient ovarian cancer. The protein could open this powerful drug class to many more patients.
plos-pone-0355965: Meat, milk, wool, and grain — animals powered medieval England’s entire economy from 400 to 1400 CE. This paper reconstructed that animal economy from archaeological and historical evidence. The sweeping economic history reveals how livestock literally built a civilization.
plos-pone-0357265: Oxygen-starved tin oxide can be tuned for electronics and hydrogen sensing. This density functional theory investigation studied oxygen-deficient SnO2-x: optoelectronic property tuning and hydrogen gas interaction. The quantum-level modeling guides the design of better sensors and devices.
plos-pone-0356765: The two eyes combine their signals seamlessly — and the combination reaches even the autonomic nervous system. This paper studied binocular combination in autonomic responses. The findings extend vision science into unexpected territory, showing the body’s unconscious systems also merge the two eyes’ input.
plos-pone-0357465: Post-COVID condition — long COVID — leaves many profoundly deconditioned. This cross-sectional study measured physical activity levels in people living with the condition. The data quantify just how far activity falls, providing a baseline for rehabilitation programs.
plos-pone-0356465: Distinguishing cervical precancer (CIN3/HSIL) from truly invasive squamous carcinoma changes everything about treatment. This interpretable Hallmark pathway activity classifier separates the two, with development and external validation. The transparent classifier aids pathologists facing genuinely hard calls.
plos-pone-0351865: Representation is contagious: seeing women in power begets more women in power. This paper demonstrated that gender representation begets gender representation — a self-reinforcing cycle. The finding reframes diversity efforts: each breakthrough doesn’t just help one woman, it multiplies.
plos-pone-0356365: Chronic pain and substance use disorders travel together far too often. This paper published a protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis of nicotine, alcohol, and cannabis use disorder prevalence among adults with chronic pain. The planned synthesis will quantify an overlap that pain clinics can no longer ignore.
plos-pone-0345965: Electroplating wastewater is a toxic cocktail demanding optimized treatment. This paper presented an integrated optimization of treatment configurations, comparing physicochemical approaches and process enhancements. The comparative assessment gives plant operators a data-driven menu for cleaning up one of industry’s nastiest effluents.
plos-pone-0354965: Millimeter-wave wireless needs beamforming that scales — and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces can help. This paper presented scalable RIS-aided hybrid beamforming for mmWave systems supporting multiple sub-array architectures, using a geometric mean approach. The scalable design brings next-generation wireless closer to affordable reality.
plos-pone-0356265: Depression and anxiety among Mozambican women follow stratified, geographic patterns — invisible without mapping. This paper charted them and drew mental health policy implications. The geographic stratification tells policymakers where to put scarce psychiatric resources for maximum impact.
plos-pone-0353565: Face recognition threatens privacy — but the technology itself might protect it. This paper enhanced face recognition privacy by integrating differential privacy with convolutional neural networks. The privacy-preserving approach lets systems recognize faces without storing the biometric details that enable abuse.
plos-pone-0356065: Root canal sealers must fill every microscopic void — and ultrasound might help them flow. This micro-CT study examined ultrasonic activation of calcium silicate sealers in single-cone obturation, mapping voids and gaps. The three-dimensional void analysis tells endodontists whether sonic agitation genuinely seals better.
plos-pone-0346465: Reef fish don’t just flee predators — they calibrate their escape to the attack. This paper showed reef fish escape responses selectively match predator attack speeds. The tuned escapes reveal split-second decision-making honed by evolution — waste no energy, miss no threat.
plos-pone-0342165: Understanding an organism’s sensors demands statistical rigor. This paper analyzed sensors using Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) models, complete with bias, variance, and confusion matrices. The principled framework reveals what sensory systems actually encode — and what they systematically get wrong.
plos-pone-0355165: Hands-off driving in a second language — cognitively loaded and risky. This paper studied pupillary dynamics during hands-off L2 driving and control transitions under high cognitive load. The pupil measurements reveal when drivers’ mental resources are maxed out — critical data for semi-autonomous vehicle safety.
plos-pone-0353465: England’s urban paradox — cities both healthier and sicker than expected — persists after the pandemic. This paper found spatial stationarity in obesity determinants in post-pandemic England. The findings challenge assumptions that COVID-19 reshaped the geography of obesity’s causes.
europmc-pmc2815665: XDS is one of the most widely used programs for processing X-ray diffraction data from crystals, and this 2010 paper is its defining reference. Written by its creator Wolfgang Kabsch, it describes how the software turns raw diffraction images into usable measurements. Generations of crystallographers learned the method from this paper. It remains the citation for a tool behind countless protein structures.
europmc-pmc2855365: The vaginal germ crowd shifts with time, and this 2010 study clocks it. The team tracks germ shifts in women and their tie to bacterial vaginosis. Their logs show which shifts spell trouble. The work aids tests that read the whole community, not just one bug.
europmc-pmc2861665: Nerve pain that lingers may be fueled by inflammation. This 2010 review examines TNF-alpha, an immune signal, in neuropathic pain. The authors gather the case for and against its role. Their weighing informs whether anti-inflammatory drugs could ease chronic nerve pain.
europmc-pmc2864565: RNA-Seq counts need scaling before genes can be compared, and this 2010 paper delivers the fix. The authors present a scaling normalization method for differential expression analysis of RNA-seq data. Their method, TMM, became a default. The paper is among the most cited in genomics.
europmc-pmc2917065: The immune drug ipilimumab offered hope in advanced melanoma. This 2010 paper reports a single hospital's compassionate-use experience, finding lymphocyte count after two doses tracks with survival. The authors' bedside clue aided early calls. Their report guided real-world use.
europmc-pmc2935965: The cell's fuel gauge, AMPK, answers to many signals through its parts. This 2010 paper uses cells carrying gamma subunit variants to tease apart the many ways AMPK switches on. The authors' toolkit dissects the gauge piece by piece. Their work clarifies how cells sense and balance energy.
europmc-pmc2987465: The cell's ribosome factory reacts to stress. This 2010 review covers how the nucleolus behaves under stress. The authors survey its shutdown and alarm signals. Their overview links nucleolar stress to disease. Cancer drugs often trip these alarms first. The review maps stress sensors in the factory.
europmc-pmc3018565: Early breast lesions got long-term answers. This 2011 trial reports years of follow-up on tamoxifen and radiation after DCIS surgery. The authors' data guides care. Their trial shaped treatment guidelines. Radiation cut recurrence risk in half. Tamoxifen helped hormone-positive cases most.
europmc-pmc3060065: Primates got a DNA-based family tree. This 2011 paper builds the primate tree from genes of living species. The authors redraw old relationships. Their work guides conservation. Lemurs branched off first, it confirms. Zoos use the tree to plan breeding.
europmc-pmc3060165: A blood microRNA flags spreading colon cancer. This 2011 paper shows blood-borne MiR-141 marks metastatic colon cancer and grim outlooks. The authors validate the marker. Their work points to blood tests. High levels meant shorter survival. Doctors may track it during treatment.
europmc-pmc3081065: Peanut allergy links to a skin gene. This 2011 paper ties broken filaggrin skin genes to peanut allergy risk. The authors reveal the link. Their work points to skin-barrier care. Cracked skin lets peanut dust sneak in. Moisturizing babies may cut the risk.
europmc-pmc6523365: Adolescence rewires how the brain handles feelings, just as anxiety and depression often first appear. This paper examines emotion regulation in teenagers - both taming bad feelings and savoring good ones - and how those skills connect to mental illness. Teens who struggle to regulate emotions face higher risk, making these skills a promising target for early intervention.
europmc-pmc6562165: Time in parks and forests feels restorative - and the data agree. Pooling studies worldwide, this meta-analysis finds greenspace exposure tied to better health: lower stress, more activity, cleaner air. The authors quantify benefits policymakers have sensed since the 1800s, making the case that green neighborhoods are health infrastructure.
europmc-pmc6562565: T cells could beat many tumors if tumors did not drug them first - cancers flood their surroundings with adenosine, a molecule that puts T cells to sleep. This review explores blocking adenosine signals to wake the immune attack back up. Early trials suggest the strategy can re-arm exhausted T cells against cancer.
europmc-pmc6570665: Clostridioides difficile - the gut germ behind brutal hospital diarrhea - strikes when antibiotics wipe out its competitors. This review covers the infection end to end: the spore-forming bacterium's tricks, why cases grew nastier over the last decade, and how doctors fight back, from targeted antibiotics to stool transplants.
europmc-pmc6598765: Mapping which proteins touch DNA - and where - got easier with CUT&RUN, a gentler alternative to older chromatin methods. This paper upgrades the toolkit: improved reagents and protocols that sharpen the maps while using fewer cells. Epigenetics researchers get crisper views of gene regulation with less hassle.
europmc-pmc6635665: Comparing many treatments at once - even ones never tested head to head - is the job of network meta-analysis. This paper teaches the method using R software, walking through Bayesian and frequentist approaches with worked examples. Researchers learn to weave scattered trials into one coherent ranking.
europmc-pmc6668865: Alcohol floods the body with reactive oxygen species - molecular sparks that scorch fats, proteins, and DNA. This classic 2003 review explains how drinking drives oxidative stress and free-radical damage. The chemistry connects the bottle to liver injury and beyond.
europmc-pmc6695865: Failing kidneys drown in oxidative stress - reactive molecules that scar tissue as function fades. This review untangles the thread: which pro-oxidant enzymes fire early in chronic kidney disease and how the damage snowballs. The Ariadne's-thread framing guides readers through a knotted literature toward therapeutic exits.
gao-gaoreports-b-310065: A formal bid-protest decision from the Government Accountability Office, dated November 21, 2007. These decisions settle disputes when a company challenges how a federal agency awarded a contract — here, a filing by NAC International, Inc. The ruling walks through the legal arguments and explains why the protest was sustained or denied, following the strict procedures Congress set for GAO's contract-review role.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-165: GAO's 2007 report on Trade Adjustment Assistance — the aid that retrains workers whose jobs moved abroad — finds the training pot shallower than the Labor Department claimed. Once spent funds and firm pledges were both counted, states had less to work with. The report warns that rosy math could shortchange the very workers the aid was built for.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1065: The visitor-tracking system was drifting in 2007 — years old, still no compass. GAO's report says the program meant to log who enters and leaves America lacked direction and sound running. The findings describe a flagship border-tech promise stuck in neutral while the debate over immigration raged around it.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-865: Treasury's tech-buying board needed a tune-up in 2007 — GAO's report says its investment watch needed stronger operations and oversight. The findings target the money-behind-the-money: who guards the guardians of the tech budget. The report demands grown-up governance for the nation's fiscal computers.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-765: The proxy advisers held quiet power in 2007 — GAO's report examines the firms telling big investors how to vote their shares. The findings pull back the curtain on the shareholder-meeting whisperers. The report asks who watches the advisers when they move billions with a recommendation.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-565: The immigration cops' computers were creaking in 2007 — GAO's report says the agency had to face its infrastructure rot head-on and soon. The findings target the neglected backbone systems in detail. The report's warning stands: you cannot enforce the border on broken machines.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-465: Food stamp rules for the jobless needed clearer guidance in 2007 — GAO's report says better monitoring would keep the noncash categories honest. The findings press for the playbook. The report's aim: benefits for those who need them, not those who game them.
gao-gaoreports-b-299165: Delaware Resource Group of Oklahoma took its February 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Every challenger gets the full hearing.
openalex-w7204107965: Postpartum depression often starts before birth, making prenatal visits a chance to catch it early. This narrative review studies how screening during pregnancy affects detection and the baby's development. The authors trace the path from checkup to outcome. A maternal-health review arguing that asking early changes lives.
openalex-w7163924565: Imagine a memory that recalls different things depending on temperature. This theoretical paper builds a simple neural-network model that retrieves one pattern when hot and another when cold, by embedding each in a different network shape. The authors show temperature flipping the recall. Playful but rigorous work on memory with a thermostat.
pmc-13492765: This 2026 paper tests a single lab test that can detect many filoviruses at once — the family that includes Ebola. The team ran the assay across different countries and resource levels to check it gives reliable results in real clinics, not just well-equipped labs. A dependable, field-ready test matters for spotting outbreaks early where they are hardest to track.
pmc-13407065: In this 2026 study, machine learning models predicted the need for tracheostomy after traumatic cervical spinal cord injury. Early tracheostomy decisions affect recovery and complications. The predictive model turns admission data into actionable foresight.
pmc-13433265: A 2026 computational paper introducing multiscale higher-order molecular simplicial complex embedding for predicting drug response. The method captures molecular relationships beyond simple pairwise connections. Richer mathematical representations could sharpen predictions of which drugs work for which patients.
pmc-13449765: In this 2026 drug discovery paper, researchers found VU6081679, a novel positive allosteric modulator of metabotropic glutamate receptor 8, with efficacy in a preclinical Parkinson's model. Fine-tuning glutamate signaling — rather than replacing dopamine — is a fresh strategy. The compound is an early but promising lead.
pmc-13402865: A 2026 mouse study finding that hepatic iron accumulation is reduced in the cholestatic Mdr2-knockout mouse — a model of bile-flow disease. Iron and bile metabolism turn out to be linked in unexpected ways. The result refines the model's use for liver disease research.
pmc-13429265: This 2026 cardiology study compared outcomes after a first heart attack in patients with versus without congenital heart disease. Adults with repaired heart defects face distinct risks. The comparison informs their long-term cardiac care.
pmc-13517465: In this 2026 animal nutrition paper, fermented forage-based mixed feed improved growth performance and meat quality in finishing pigs. Fermentation upgrades forage value. The feeding trial gives producers data.
pmc-13424465: This 2026 randomized trial provided preliminary safety data on early versus standard timing of measles-rubella vaccination in Ugandan infants. Earlier protection could save lives. The safety data are the first step.
pmc-13530765: This 2026 conference poster found the glenoid track width smaller under dynamic loading during daily activities, in a finite element analysis. The shoulder's stability margin shrank in motion. The poster reports the simulation.
pmc-13516765: A 2026 protocol combining questionnaire-based stratification and wearable home sleep testing for screening sleep-disordered breathing risk in pediatric dental care. The dental chair became a screening site. The protocol is the innovation.
pmc-13499265: This 2026 systems biology paper explored nonlinearities and switch-like behavior in gene expression — from genetics to biochemistry and back. The gene circuits behaved like switches. The exploration connects scales.
pmc-13498865: This 2026 plant paper showed the SlARF6A-SlFBA3/SlSGR module regulates tomato resistance to Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato. The genetic module conferred defense. The regulation is the mechanism.
